Ahmed S.N., Bertorini T.E., Narayanaswami P. et al. Clinical approach to a patient presenting with muscle stiffness. Journal of Clinical Neuromuscular Disease. 2003;4(3):150-160.

Educational Objectives: 1. To learn to evaluate a patient presenting with muscle stiffness. 2. To be familiar with the clinical features that differentiate the various disorders presenting with muscle stiffness. 3. To understand the diagnostic work-up of these patients. 4. To correlate the electrophysiological findings in each condition with this clinical presentation. A 41-year-old right-handed African-American woman presented with gradual onset of stiffness and painful spasms affecting her right lower extremity. The stiffness was persistent and progressive. The spasms were precipitated by sudden noise, anxiety, or fear. Her gait was impaired as a result of the stiffness and spasms and she subsequently suffered from falls. After several weeks she developed similar symptoms in the left lower extremity and her axial musculature, with significant stiffness of her lower back.

extractions.value: The pertinent clinical finding was the rock-like hardness of abdominal and paraspinal muscles on palpation, and exaggerated lumbar lordosis. Serum islet-cell cytoplasmic antibodies were elevated. EMG revealed continuous motor unit activity in the absence of volitional contraction of muscles. The administration of diazepam abolished this activity.
extractions.quote: The pertinent clinical finding was the rock-like hardness of abdominal and paraspinal muscles on palpation, and exaggerated lumbar lordosis. Serum islet-cell cytoplasmic antibodies were elevated. EMG revealed continuous motor unit activity in the absence of volitional contraction of muscles. The administration of diazepam abolished this activity. There was no myokymia or myotonia. Thus, the history, clinical presentation, laboratory, and EMG findings were consistent with a diagnosis of SPS.
